output.name: Tesmal — the Gull That Stays
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, a gull was still on it. Ennu had made her that spring from sailcloth and goose bone, and she was the best flier on the cliffs. Tavo came in off the sea, laughed, and took her up, and the string went slack in Hesk's hands. Hesk counted the loss and marked it on the Reel. The gull did not fall. She rode up into Vel, wings spread, and she sits there yet, high in the north, beside the Loosed Gull that Kael's net brought up fishing for a fallen star. To the south, the Asking Raven puts her questions to the wind: is the herring running, where does the string end? The Gulls, who are her cousins, say the gull keeps her head turned toward home. Each spring a cliff-wife ties a scrap of cloth to a kite and flies it for her. If the scrap comes back down the wind, she has heard. If it does not, she has kept it, which is also an answer. Mend your own lines before you ask the sky for more.
output.finding: Find the Loosed Gull in the north-west of the Windward Reach, then look nearly one hand-span to the south-east of it for the Gull That Stays.
